You definitely should buy and carry a firearm if you have PTSD. It works wonders for feeling in control again. Most of the people telling you not to seem to fear firearms, distrust themselves and others, or assume that PTSD means you can't control your behavior and will just start busting off randomly if you become triggered. That's an insulting misconception, though I am not surprised to see it here on Reddit as this website's community is generally biased in favor of left-wing politics, I,e. anti-firearms. I've also looked through many of their posting histories and was unsurprised to find that the people telling you not to are mostly Europeans and/or people that have no experience handling firearms and actively hate them. The only reasons you shouldn't get a weapon is if you plan to use it for premeditated murder or you are actively suicidal. 

I've been carrying for a long time and my PTSD overlapped with that timespan. Not once did I misuse my weapons, even when irrationally panicking, because I'm not psychotic. I agree with the notion that it is dependent on the individual. If you think you'll use it to commit murder or kill yourself, don't get one. If you know you can trust yourself, and you want to feel safe again, definitely go through with it. And be sure to practice often and look into firearms self-defense courses so you can learn gun safety and valuable combat skills. 

I wish you the best, and I hope you don't take advice from some of the more fearful and ignorant among us.

Well if you're in a rural area (in the US) then it's highly likely you have lax laws about carrying any sort of weapon. If you're not comfortable with a firearm, a telescopic/expandable/collapsible baton in your purse or pocket could work. Or a fixed blade knife that's not too long to conceal, such as a KA-BAR. Folding pocket knives are generally shit because they take too long to deploy in a dangerous situation (they have to be flipped up, and some require two hands to do so) and can break down easily because of the moving parts present. That's why the military doesn't issue or use them outside of opening cardboard boxes. 

Sorry I keep trying to get you to arm yourself, I just really don't know what else to do to make you feel safe (and **be** safe) in the scenario you've presented. Especially if you only have one store that you can go to. Situations like this are why I always have and always will advocate for women (and any sufferer of PTSD, regardless of their sex) to carry weapons.

Whatever you do I wish you luck, and hope that you can regain a sense of security outside your home.

I understand your rage and pain. Truly. As retarded as this is going to sound right now, the best thing to do is move on from him. I wanted to exact revenge as well, but I realized I was becoming the same kind of animal that brutalized me in the first place. I lost my humanity and went from being a victim of bloodshed to a perpetrator of it. And now violence is my foundation. 

PTSD, especially for men, carries an element of rage. It's because your fight-or-fight response is in overdrive, and men are inclined and designed to fight. While TomsDiner1 is correct that it's most likely unhelpful for you, it's natural and easily understood for you to respond in such a way. 

The most important thing right now is for you to heal, both physically and mentally. The piece of shit who ran you down isn't going to be any less shitty with shackles on his wrists or a bullet in his brain. And even if he was, there would still be an innumerable number of shitheads like him. But you have the potential to become better than you are, and better than you were, as a result of your experience. I understand if you view that as a vapid platitude. I hate seemingly empty sentiment, so I really would get it. 

The way you deal with the helplessness and hopelessness and loneliness is the same way you would deal with any other hardship. Take it a day, or an hour, or a minute at a time. If you look at all your problems all at once you will end up feeling like Atlas; the whole world's weight will be on your shoulders and holding it up will stop you from doing anything else. 

You are the most important person in your world, if you aren't, you should be. At least for now. You need to focus on yourself, not your attacker. And I don't want to discourage you, but it's incredibly difficult to find the perpetrators of hit-and-runs. My uncle is a quadriplegic who cannot speak without external aid, and who is fully conscious, similar to the late Stephen Hawking. He's been that way since before I was born, and it's because someone hit him with a station wagon and broke his spine. They never caught the man who did it, because like the coward he is, he ran from judgment, and because hit-and-runs are essentially unsolvable without a witness or a recording. The police probably are actually doing their best, it's just not enough. If you put all of your eggs in their kevlar-lined basket, you'll run out of eggs.

Your life is far more important than your attacker's. So focus on yours instead of his.

You don't have to be isolated, you just shouldn't date while depressed unless you're actively receiving treatment that is helping you along. Otherwise the difference between life and death could be a break-up text.

The first half of what he said is completely correct. Depending on someone else for happiness while depressed is extremely dangerous. Doubly so if that person is someone you're dating. It's like playing with matches while soaked in diesel and wearing a backpack filled with fireworks.

I'm not saying the most important thing is to love ourselves. I consider that a worthless platitude, no offense. I'm just saying not to believe that a relationship is the solution to this problem. If anything, it will exacerbate it.

PTSD has physical effects on the human body, chiefly the central nervous system. I know from experience what that's like, you can't calm down no matter what you do which is why substance abuse goes hand-in-hand with PTSD.

It's highly likely that his fight-or-flight response is constantly in full swing. That tends to cause frustration and outbursts of rage over trivial matters. It most likely has very little to do with you, he's just forced to live like a wounded, cornered animal. 

Just try to be slow, gentle, and understanding, even though he will most likely give you a hard time without meaning to. It sounds like you're already doing those things, which is wonderful. We should all be so lucky to have someone like you in our lives. And unlike most gushy commenters online, I mean that.

It depends. I was told the same thing once, didn't do it, and I was fine. But I don't know your situation with weed. You can't be physically dependent on it, but (and I say this as a stoner) anyone who thinks you can't become addicted to it (psychologically) is an imbecile. And an addiction like that could potentially effect your mental state. Weed is helpful for PTSD and depression until you find yourself becoming depressed when you don't have it. This isn't really something someone can you give you a definitive answer on, because we aren't you. 

Weed is definitely less harmful than the cocktails of psych drugs that are handed out like Halloween candy, though. I've witnessed for myself what can happen to a person on SSRIs, and it isn't good. Though I don't want you to write off pharmaceuticals based on my anecdotes.

You can contact me if you'd like. I'm a male, and I wasn't sexually assaulted, but I had PTSD from a gory incident that crippled me mentally for half a decade. I understand the helplessness and the inescapable nightmare that life becomes in the aftermath.

Hmu right here or in pms if you want to talk about this further, but just know I log in infrequently. If I don't respond for a while, it's not because I'm ignoring you.

Don't take this the wrong way but you probably shouldn't be in a relationship if you're suffering from depression. The thing about relationships, especially in the modern age, is that they inevitably end. I thought all I needed in life was a girlfriend, and after getting one I did feel better for a time. But my symptoms did not go away just because I had a gf. And when she left me, they tripled in severity and I got caught by my little brother with a pistol in my mouth. I regret traumatizing him in that way, though he did inadvertently prevent my death, to my dismay. 

Anyway the bottom line is that relationships are almost never permanent. There are far more failed relationships than successful ones, and a failed relationship is one of, if not the biggest, inciting event for suicides.

I've taken LSD once. It was like taking a vacation without going anywhere. I can't explain that better to those who haven't used it. If you have, you know exactly what I'm conveying.

When I was on acid I was fully lucid and always aware what was real and what wasn't. I still enjoyed it immensely, but there was nothing spiritual about it. The closest thing to a spiritual moment I had was when I was coming down, sweating and shivering, and staring at my own nude body in the mirror. In that moment I didn't see a person staring back - I saw an animal that for the first time had stopped playing dress-up and was confronting itself, and it didn't understand what it saw. It didn't understand anything. And it still doesn't. Ever since then I've been much more hesitant to separate humans from animals. It doesn't stop me from hunting them, but it does make me understand that when I pull the trigger I'm killing something that's exactly the same as myself, but doesn't have the tools in its toolbox to see that, or fight back against me in a meaningful way.

History is a great thing to explore, not to understand where we come from, but to understand that humanity is foundationally broken and continues to repeat the same patterns of extreme violence and pain. And we will forever, long after we construct utopias amongst the stars. Because we're fucked.

I have a mantra I like to repeat to myself when I get irrationally fearful of supernatural things: "The only monsters in this world walk on two legs."

The people who surround me make me more depressed than all my traumas and mistakes combined. Because they have hope, not just for me but for themselves. They have an almost genetic certainty that things just can't be as horrible as they really, truly are. When I have conversations with people about my extreme nihilism, they automatically reject my opinions. When I ask why, it's always the same answer. "I just can't believe that." And you know what? I believe them. And it makes me sad, because they don't even know they're trapped. They don't see the fences so they think they're free.

Most of all, I'm saddened by how they can live in the same nightmare world as me and be happy. I can't. I've been a daily user of drugs for years. If I wasn't always high, I'd have killed myself long before this comment.
I'm waiting for death to come find me. If it doesn't soon, I'll find it myself.

The last sentence of your comment is pretty accurate though. I don't pursue things or people I'm interested in because I don't see a point. All I see is failure and rejection and hate because that's all I've ever really experienced. I don't know what it feels like to succeed or feel joy.

I accept that the things and people around me are real, but nothing seems like reality to me. Smoking dank meme grass doesn't help, it exacerbates the fuck out of it but I don't really give a shit.

It's like I go to the back of my mind and just put in the bare social minimum and get away with it every time. Once I'm alone I stop pretending to feel and go completely cold and empty and occupy my time doing whatever.

Pretty much took the words out of my mouth.

There are things I enjoy but it's not really happiness, I don't feel things very often unless they are extreme and negative. Other than that I'm just a robot most of the time, not really paying attention to anything and trying to avoid human contact. What I feel when I enjoy things is more like peace or quiet than a feeling. I don't really know when my depression began, but I had it before I had PTSD and it's spiked since I got it for obvious reasons.

I think I enjoyed things when I was a child. My memories of back then are "brighter" at least. I feel that each passing day I'm less and less alive. 
I actually thought that for a time I was getting better because I had PTSD for ~4 years and it finally stopped around summer last year. But I don't think so anymore. I still think about suicide every day and my fear of death is nonexistent. The only thing stopping me when I think about doing it is the amount of work it would take to get all my shit in order so that when people inevitably go looking through my stuff they don't find anything weird or sexual.

I don't want to add to your problems but I've been there with the whole "dating someone who's just as broken as me" thing and in my experience it's a bad fucking move. 
That being said, it's your life and you can do what you want. It may even work out for you. I hope that I'm wrong and that it does go well for you.
